title: Batch 6, revision 3: technical readiness and usefulness of the autonomous Jira/PR impact service on synthetic stands, after the Jira route-negation fix, with complete human-minute coverage and live model configurations defined before any model run
frozen_before: any held-out run of 6-r3 in any configuration; the 6-r3 development worlds were generated while the wording was written; the 6-r3 held-out names, keys and seeds are new

unit.change: one Jira issue and the PR that implements it, on its own Git stand and its own fresh service installation; the Jira issue and the PR are one unit, not two
unit.stage: the Jira comment or the PR comment of one change
unit.consumer_pair: (change, consumer service) with an oracle severity; pairs of one change are correlated, their intervals are optimistic
unit.negative_pair: (change, service) that the oracle marks as not affected: decoy provider, decoy callers, bystanders of an unchanged operation, consumers of an unchanged route
unit.resource: one Jira issue or one PR, for publication integrity

development.use: allowed for tuning prompts, parameters and the service; rerunnable

heldout.use: never for tuning; run once per configuration after the manifest commit; the runner refuses a stale manifest and an existing held-out ledger

sample_size.decision: 22 development and 70 held-out independent changes: the 6-r2 sizes plus one F14 world per development set and five per held-out set, so every family keeps 5 held-out changes
reasoning: The gate rates (useful autonomous output, failure, wrong confident answer) are change-level and independent; at n=60 the 95% interval is within +-0.11 for rates near 0.7 and +-0.06 near 0.95, enough to tell a usable service (>=0.7) from a coin flip (0.5): their intervals do not overlap.

Zero-tolerance counters (lost, duplicate, stale publications, revoked leaks) over 120 resources bound the per-resource rate below 0.031 when zero is observed (rule of three: 3/120 = 0.025); over 60 changes below 0.060.
Per-family results (5 changes each) are descriptive only; no claim is made per family.

A service-versus-baseline difference is paired on the same 60 changes; an unpaired worst case needs about 0.18 to be distinguishable, so the comparison gate asks for at least 0.10 and is reported with both intervals, not as a significance claim.

More changes would narrow intervals but the stands are synthetic: precision beyond +-0.1 on synthetic worlds says nothing more about company data. The next evidence step is company history, not a larger synthetic set.

families.F01_truncation: default page size decreases; single-request consumers break, cursor and explicit-page-size consumers need a recheck; a same-named decoy provider and its caller are present
families.F02_operation_removed: the operation is removed; every consumer breaks
families.F03_no_impact_noop: README or docs-only change; Jira names the provider service (three wordings, the API stated unchanged in two, nothing about the API in one) or nothing; nobody is affected
families.F04_no_consumer_operation: the changed operation has no consumers; consumers of another operation of the same provider are not affected
families.F05_runtime_only: a consumer takes its URL from deployment configuration that no readable repository holds; only fresh access logs show the call
families.F06_code_only: a runtime source is configured but does not show one of the code consumers
families.F07_stale_runtime: as F05, but the only access-log window is two days old (older than the 24 h runtime freshness limit)
families.F08_revoked_source: one consumer repository was readable earlier and is revoked now; it is affected but must never be shown
families.F09_ownership_conflict: one affected consumer has two owner teams, one has none in the mapping
families.F10_ambiguous_jira: two providers declare the same route and the Jira text names neither: abstaining is correct at Jira; the PR identifies the provider
families.F11_vague_jira: the Jira text names no route and no service: abstaining is correct at Jira
families.F12_unclassified_change: the declaration body changes in a way no classifier covers; consumers need a recheck, a partial answer is correct
families.F13_service_contract_unspecified: as F01 on the PR; the Jira text names the provider and a contract change (page size, response, smaller portions) but not the operation: candidates or an abstention are correct at Jira, a confident answer is not
families.F14_route_stated_unchanged: the PR changes only documentation; the Jira text names the provider operation only to state that it does not change (Russian and English, one paraphrase that names the route without a change verb); expected: Jira no_impact, PR no_impact

every_world: a provider with the changed operation and an unchanged count operation; 1-2 bystanders of the count operation; ownership mapping for every service; names, task keys and repository bytes of the two splits are disjoint

oracle.source: execution: every consumer's load_day runs against a recording fake of requests with the providers as on main and as on the PR branch (oracle.py); the service, the static extractor, the baseline and any model take no part

severity.breaking: calls the changed operation and its result differs after the change (fewer records or an HTTP error)
severity.recheck: calls the changed operation and its result is the same
severity.none: does not call the changed operation

oracle.owner_status: from the ownership mapping: one team KNOWN, several CONFLICT, none UNKNOWN
oracle.basis: code for clients whose URL is a constant; runtime or stale_runtime for clients whose URL comes from deployment configuration, by the age of the newest access-log window that shows them

outcome_rules.jira: abstain when the text does not identify the operation (ambiguous route or no mention); candidate when the text names the provider and a contract change but not the operation; no_impact when no consumer is affected; partial when some affected consumer has only a runtime basis; otherwise answer
outcome_rules.pr: no_impact when no consumer is affected; partial for an unclassified change or when some affected consumer has only a runtime basis; otherwise answer

oracle.isolation: the oracle files are read only by scorer.py and the corpus tests; the runner and the baseline receive change files and stands only, and run with the oracle directory absent (tested)

scoring.stage_correct: status acceptable, no missed expected consumer, no false positive, no revoked service in the result or comment text, every expected consumer with the right provider operation (and on the PR stage the right call site for code consumers), owner status as in the mapping, a stale-only consumer never shown with only CURRENT freshness, on the PR stage severity exactly as the oracle for code-basis consumers (runtime-basis consumers: see pr_runtime_basis)
scoring.useful_autonomous: per change: Jira stage correct, PR stage correct, publication intact (one comment per resource, current body digest, delivered, no write after redelivery), no crash
scoring.outcome_classes: answer (USEFUL), partial (PARTIAL), abstain (ABSTAINED), failure (FAILED, no result or crash), counted separately per stage
scoring.latency: seconds from the webhook delivery to the last accepted comment write of that stage, local stands; worker polling is synchronous in the runner
scoring.graph_freshness: after the merge (provider default branch moves to the PR head) one periodic reconciliation: the provider's git source version equals the head and the active declared operations equal the head's
scoring.publication: lost: no comment or the newest result intent not DELIVERED; duplicate: more than one service comment or create; stale: comment digest differs from the newest generation's body or the published generation is behind; plus writes caused by a redelivered webhook
scoring.cost: model calls and tokens from AnalysisResult.costs; roubles only when every call has a price; no-model configuration has none
scoring.human_minutes: Recorded inputs only, with who recorded them and how (recorded_by, method). Usage minutes per change and setup minutes of the installation are separate. The usage median is reported and gated only when every expected change of the split (the oracle's change ids, so a change that never ran stays in the denominator) has a recorded value; otherwise the human gate is INCOMPLETE and only the lower bound of the median (missing values as zero) is shown, with a diagnostic when that bound already exceeds the limit. A recorded zero counts; a missing value is unknown. Machine wall time and zero interventions are not human minutes. The runner has no human step; synthetic changes are not labelled by the owner to make this gate pass.
scoring.pr_runtime_basis_meaning: On the PR stage a consumer whose only basis is runtime (its URL comes from deployment configuration that no readable repository holds) must be named with the changed provider operation and with freshness that is not CURRENT when its only window is stale. Its severity is not required and it leaves the breaking-as-breaking denominator (T18): the oracle's severity comes from executing code the service cannot read, and the service's profile assigns severity only from a call site's usage. Asking for 'breaking' would reward turning traffic into a proven break. The pairs get their own threshold (T30). The oracle's severities themselves are unchanged.
scoring.candidate_stage: Jira stage with expected outcome candidate: correct when the status is PARTIAL or ABSTAINED, nothing revoked leaks and nothing stale is shown as current; USEFUL is a wrong confident answer (T23). Named services that the oracle marks as not affected count in the Jira FP rate (T22) but do not make the stage wrong, because the result labels them as unconfirmed candidates. There is no recall requirement at this stage.

service-no-model.freshness: graph query defaults: runtime 86400 s, ownership 604800 s

service-model.status: runs only after preflight: the qualification reference (2B report path, run_id, SHA-256) passes agent_service.qualification.check against the loaded constitution, code and the model profile built from the 2B program; on any mismatch the run is refused before a model call and the reason code is printed; never with a model admitted by a flag
service-model.analyzer: CoreAnalyzer with the 2B model profile and the qualification reference; same stands and runner
service-model.model_profile: 2B program 2b-r1: endpoint, parameters and the model's max_completion_tokens; limits.max_tool_lines 60
service-model.cost: tokens from AnalysisResult.costs; roubles from the 2B model price; unknown usage stays unknown
service-model.stop: the series stops after two consecutive changes whose model calls all failed, or at the series deadline; the remaining changes are recorded as not run and stay in every denominator

baseline-live.status: runs only with the model and endpoint of the service-model configuration it is compared with
baseline-live.protocol: baseline-search-1 over CloudRuTransport; its search prompt and actions differ from actions-v3 by design, so the 2B qualification of actions-v3 is no evidence about the quality of this prompt
baseline-live.limits: baseline LIMITS: 12 steps, 120 s per stage, max_completion_tokens of the model (4096); the service model runs under the constitution limits; both are recorded in the ledger binding
baseline-live.stop: as service-model; an unauthorised or rate-limited transport stops the series at once

baseline-naive-search.status: runnable offline; harness check and floor, not a model

one updatable comment per resource
the comment shows the newest generation
a redelivered webhook writes nothing
a revoked source is never shown
a revoked source is never shown
stale evidence is never shown as current
stale evidence is never shown as current
technical failures are rare
technical failures are rare
a Jira insight within a minute on local stands
a PR insight within a minute on local stands
a merged change is in the graph after one reconciliation
reconciliation of a small installation is fast
most changes need no human correction of the comments
the interval excludes a coin flip
breaking consumers with a code basis are reported as breaking; runtime-basis consumers are scored by T30 (see scoring.pr_runtime_basis_meaning)
the preliminary insight names who may be affected
the path names the right operation and call site
PR comments rarely name unaffected services
the preliminary insight may be wider, but not much
no confident answer where abstaining or no impact is correct; 6-r2: stages with expected candidate count too
no confident answer where no impact is correct
owners are not guessed
owners are not guessed

verdict_rules.technical_readiness: gate technical PASS on the held-out ledger of the configuration
verdict_rules.usefulness_on_synthetic_stands: gate quality PASS on the held-out ledger; this is not business usefulness
verdict_rules.business_usefulness: UNVERIFIED in this program: it needs company history (real changes, real consumers, real incidents) and recorded human minutes; no synthetic result can establish it
verdict_rules.gate_states: PASS when every threshold passes, FAIL when any fails, INCOMPLETE when any is NOT_MEASURED or NOT_EVALUATED

evidence_levels: L1 synthetic Git stand: generated repositories, execution-grounded oracle (this program)
L2 local HTTP stand: the real service, webhook receiver, queue and connectors against local GitHub/Jira emulations on 127.0.0.1 (this program)
L3 real integration: GitHub App, Jira Cloud test project, VM installation (not in this program)
L4 company data: real repositories, history, consumers and people (not in this program)

relation_to_earlier_revisions.historical: 6-r1 (manifest 6140e378, FAIL) and 6-r2 (manifest 45f49527, technical and quality PASS without a model, human and comparison INCOMPLETE) keep their programs, corpora, ledgers and verdicts; their scoring rules are read from their own program.json
relation_to_earlier_revisions.not_comparable: 6-r1 47/60 and 6-r2 65/65 were scored under different rules on different corpora; neither is an improvement measured on an unchanged benchmark, and 6-r3 is not either
fixes_measured: Jira intent: a route named only as unchanged is no target; the rest of the text decides (src/agent_service/intent.py, review of #64 on 26.10.2026)
human gate: complete coverage of the split before a median counts (scoring.human_coverage)
relation_to_earlier_revisions.regression_examples: the 26.10 review cases (route stated unchanged, 1 of 65 minutes) are regression tests in tests/service and tools/autonomous_mvp/tests; passing them is not held-out evidence
relation_to_earlier_revisions.new_heldout: 70 changes drawn from seeds 6-r3:heldout:<i>, with names and Jira keys in no split of 6-r1 or 6-r2
relation_to_earlier_revisions.prepared_by: the same executor (Claude) that wrote the fixes, the generator and the oracle rules, on 27.10.2026; no independent author wrote or reviewed the texts before the freeze
relation_to_earlier_revisions.known_bias: the 6-r3 wording (negated routes, paraphrases, English) was written after the route-negation fix by its author: it checks these phrasings, not how people write tasks; new seeds and names do not remove that bias. One F14 paraphrase names the route without a change verb, which the deterministic matcher is known to read as a change; it stays in the set as a stated limitation, not a tuned case
